document.abstract: Current innovations in compression technology allow for the storage of high-definition format video on the same format cassette that is used for standard definition. This is done using MPEG-2 compression. To achieve high rates of compression, MPEG-2 uses a groups of pictures (GOP) method with a single intraframe (I frame), complete picture information, predictive (P frames), and bidirectional frames (B frames) that are dependent on context to create a complete image. Bit for bit, this MPEG-2 stream puts greater demands on data transfer integrity during playback in order to decode and reconstruct each and every frame in the GOP as they were originally encoded. This requires a technologically advanced tape media. In this paper, the methods for making metal-evaporated tape media capable of meeting this need will be discussed.

authors.bio: Wayne Desmond joined Sony Electronics Inc. in 2002 and is currently senior manager technical training, Media and Application Solutions Div. He started his career with RKO Tape Corp. in 1981, heading up QC Operations from 1983 to 1988. From 1988 to 2002, he worked in the Magnetic Tape Div. of Agfa Corp. and BASF Corp. as technical support engineer and senior engineer, respectively.
authors.name: Wayne Desmond

authors.bio: Hideki Kikuchi joined Sony in 1981 and is currently senior manager of quality development in the Tape Media Div. in the Recording Media and Device Business Group. He is responsible for in-house tape media quality and worldwide customer support. His background includes professional tape development-making and business promotion.
authors.name: Hideki Kikuchi

authors.bio: Steven Tice joined Sony Magnetic Products of America in 1980 and is currently senior manager of customer service engineering, responsible for customer support of professional, data, and consumer magnetic and optical media, memory storage devices, and biometric products for the Americas Zone. He also manages the Sony Media Warranty Center and Sony Media Services Groups. His background includes broadcast electronics and systems support and direct customer field support for recording media.
authors.name: Steve Tice
